difficultyReason: Methodological/scientific argument where the correct answer confirms a load-bearing assumption about study design. Distractors include a plausible-but-irrelevant fact about the drug class and a choice that strengthens a neighboring claim rather than the core conclusion.
stimulus: A clinical study followed two groups of patients with elevated cholesterol for three years. One group took a newly developed plant-based supplement daily; the other group took a placebo. At the end of the study, the supplement group showed a 15 percent greater reduction in LDL cholesterol than the placebo group. The researchers concluded that the supplement itself caused the additional reduction in LDL cholesterol.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The plant extract used in the supplement has been shown to inhibit cholesterol synthesis in isolated liver cells.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Participants in both groups reported no significant changes in diet or exercise habits over the course of the study.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Plant-based supplements are generally considered safer than synthetic cholesterol-lowering drugs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The researchers who conducted the study have previously published research on plant-based medicines.

choices.label: E
choices.text: LDL cholesterol levels naturally decline in some patients over a three-year period without any intervention.

explanations.correct: The argument's conclusion rests on the supplement being the cause of the difference. A rival explanation is that the supplement group independently changed diet or exercise habits. (B) eliminates that rival explanation by confirming lifestyle habits were stable across both groups, directly supporting the causal claim.
explanations.A: This confirms a possible biological mechanism, but it strengthens a neighboring claim about how the supplement could work in theory — not the conclusion that it actually caused the observed reduction in this study. Strengthens a different conclusion.
explanations.B: Correct. Rules out a confounding lifestyle variable, closing the most salient gap between the observed difference and the causal conclusion.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant — safety comparisons to synthetic drugs have no bearing on whether the supplement caused LDL reduction.
explanations.D: Irrelevant; the researchers' prior publication record does not speak to whether the supplement caused the outcome in this study.
explanations.E: Introduces an alternative explanation — natural decline — which would weaken the argument by suggesting the supplement group's improvement may not have been caused by the supplement.

difficultyReason: Economic/policy argument built on an analogy between two jurisdictions. The correct answer closes the analogical gap by confirming a structural similarity. Distractors include an unwarranted comparison and a choice that would actually weaken by suggesting the jurisdictions differ in a relevant way.
stimulus: When the city of Harwell reduced its downtown parking fees by 40 percent three years ago, retail sales in the downtown corridor increased by 18 percent within twelve months. The city of Calderton is now considering the same fee reduction. Proponents argue that Calderton's downtown retail sector will therefore likely experience a similar boost in sales.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, provides the most support for the proponents' argument?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Surveys show that parking cost is one of the primary reasons residents of Calderton avoid shopping downtown.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Harwell's downtown retailers credited the parking fee reduction as the main cause of their increased revenue.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Several cities that reduced downtown parking fees saw no appreciable change in retail sales.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Calderton's downtown retail sector is larger and more diversified than Harwell's was at the time of its fee reduction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reducing parking fees is a less expensive policy intervention than constructing new parking structures.

explanations.correct: The analogical argument requires that parking cost be a deterrent to Calderton shoppers — that the mechanism driving Harwell's results also operates in Calderton. (A) directly confirms that deterrence is present in Calderton, closing the key analogical gap.
explanations.A: Correct. Confirms that the mechanism behind Harwell's success — parking cost discourages downtown visits — applies to Calderton, making the predicted outcome more likely.
explanations.B: Strengthens the claim that the fee reduction caused Harwell's results, which is a neighboring claim already accepted in the argument. It does not address whether the same effect will occur in Calderton — strengthens a different conclusion.
explanations.C: Weakens the argument by introducing counterexamples where the policy failed, undercutting the reliability of the analogy.
explanations.D: Introduces a disanalogy — Calderton's sector is structurally different — which might suggest the outcomes will differ rather than converge. This could weaken rather than strengthen.
explanations.E: Accurate but irrelevant; cost-effectiveness comparisons among policy options don't support the prediction that sales will increase.

difficultyReason: Environmental science argument with a causal claim about species decline. The correct answer confirms an implicit mechanism. Trap (D) sounds supportive but addresses a general principle rather than the specific causal claim; trap (E) is a disguised weakener.
stimulus: Over the past two decades, populations of a freshwater mussel species in the Teller River basin have declined by more than 60 percent. During that same period, agricultural runoff containing elevated levels of phosphorus has increased substantially in the basin. Biologists studying the mussel populations concluded that the phosphorus-laden runoff is the primary cause of the decline.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the biologists' conclusion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Laboratory experiments show that mussels of this species experience significantly higher mortality rates when exposed to phosphorus concentrations matching those now found in the Teller River.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Phosphorus runoff from agriculture has increased in river basins throughout the region over the same two-decade period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Freshwater mussels are considered a keystone species because their decline can trigger broader ecosystem disruption.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Elevated phosphorus levels are known to harm a wide variety of freshwater invertebrate species.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A dam constructed upstream in the Teller River basin fifteen years ago has altered the river's flow rate and sediment composition.

explanations.correct: The biologists' conclusion requires that phosphorus at the levels now present in the Teller River actually harms this mussel species. (A) provides direct experimental evidence of precisely that mechanism — mortality increases at exactly those concentrations — confirming the implicit causal link.
explanations.A: Correct. Confirms the biological mechanism at the specific phosphorus concentrations present in this case, directly supporting the causal conclusion.
explanations.B: Indicates the phenomenon is widespread, but does not establish that phosphorus caused the Teller River declines specifically. A regional trend does not rule out other local factors unique to the Teller basin.
explanations.C: Accurate but irrelevant — the ecological importance of mussels says nothing about what is causing their decline in this basin.
explanations.D: Strengthens a general claim that phosphorus harms freshwater invertebrates broadly, but does not confirm that this particular species is harmed at the concentrations in the Teller River. Strengthens a neighboring, more general conclusion rather than the specific one.
explanations.E: Introduces an alternative causal explanation — altered flow and sediment from a dam — that could account for the decline without implicating phosphorus runoff. This is a disguised weakener.
